findings.F1: The tested fade is real and lasts one day only. In falling markets, wide up days that close in the top quarter were followed by a next-day excess return of −1.26 % (t −2.32, 324 cases on 141 days), and the book's cases gave +0.98 % short (t 2.09, 178 days). Over days 2–3 the short gave −0.41 % (t −0.74), and over 3 days it gave +0.61 % (t 0.84), so the whole move is in the first day.
findings.F2: The fade is strongest when the wide up day comes right after a sharp fall. Among the cases, the third with the weakest prior 5-day return gave +2.85 % short next day (t 2.48, 114 cases on 59 days). The middle third gave −0.15 % (t −0.29) and the top third +0.40 % (t 0.60). This tercile split is one of about 80 groups looked at, so it is suggestive rather than decisive.
findings.F3: The fade belongs to falling markets. In rising markets the same wide, high-close up days were followed by +0.61 % (t 1.07, 166 days), the side opposite a fade. In choppy markets they were followed by −0.65 % (t −0.96).
findings.F4: The book's own grading does not work. The third of cases with the strongest forecast gave only +0.49 % short (t 0.64, 58 days), against +1.21 % (t 1.64) and +1.24 % (t 2.38) for the weaker two thirds. Among all falling-market up days, the next-day result levels off at width quintiles 2 to 4 (−0.87 %, −0.73 %, −0.91 %) after quintiles 0 and 1 near 0.
findings.F5: Relative volume orders the cases. The third with the lowest volume against its 20-day mean gave +0.07 % short (t 0.11, 78 days), against +1.59 % (t 2.17) and +1.64 % (t 1.93) for the middle and highest thirds.
findings.F6: The book fails as a book because its edge sits in a few days. It was non-zero on 316 days, its 10 best days made 153 % of its summed return, and its daily returns had a correlation of −0.52 with the coins'. It earned a Sharpe of 0.47, which is −0.14 below holding the coins.

ideas.idea: In a falling market, a wide up day that comes after a sharp fall over the coin's previous 5 days is followed by a fall over the next day. The deeper the previous 5-day fall, the larger the next day's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should sell for one day into the wide bounces that follow a fresh drop in a downtrend, and leave alone the wide up days that come after a quiet or rising week.
ideas.name: falling drop bounce fade

ideas.idea: In a falling market, a wide up day traded on heavy volume against the coin's 20-day average volume is followed by a fall over the next day. The heavier that day's volume against its 20-day average, the larger the next day's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should fade the heavy-volume relief rallies of a downtrend for one day, and refuse to fade the thin-volume ones.
ideas.name: falling heavy volume bounce fade
